title: Ten-Year Outcomes of LASIK for Pediatric Myopic Anisometropia

license.statement: CC BY-NC 3.0 (article <license>: Dove Medical Press terms incorporating the Creative Commons Attribution - Non Commercial (unported, v3.0) License)

indication: high myopic anisometropic amblyopia in children aged 4-12 years (interocular SER difference of at least 6.00 D), after mandatory 6-month occlusion or penalization; retrospective series with 10-year follow-up

groups.description: unilateral LASIK of the amblyopic eye (Moria M2 microkeratome 130 um flap, Nidek EC-5000 CX II, ablation depth at most 120 um) mostly under general anaesthesia; 32 operated eyes of 32 children who completed 10 years of follow-up; emmetropia targeted in the affected eyes (Results)

series.notes: mean ± SD of the operated eyes (asterisks mark tests against baseline); visits 6 months, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 years; all 32 eyes completed 10 years of follow-up (inclusion criterion)

exclusions.reason: interocular difference, not the SE of operated eyes
same preoperative reference as t0002!R2C3 (not duplicated)

exclusions.what: t0001 range rows and the Table 2 footnote/Results text values
exclusions.reason: ranges and text values (protocol inclusion 4); the tabulated means are cited

notes: Target: Methods state the goal of emmetropia within the LASIK treatment limit, otherwise anisometropia reduction to 2.00 D or less; Results state that corneal thickness allowed targeting of emmetropia in the affected eyes; recorded as plano.
Refraction: cycloplegic and manifest refraction (retinoscopy and subjective trial) were measured at every visit; Table 2 does not state which SER is tabulated; recorded as unstated.
Analysis set: children who completed 10 years of follow-up and the treatment plan (attendance/compliance-based, not outcome-defined; kept).
One eye had an incomplete flap (halted microkeratome); its LASIK was performed 6 months later with a deeper flap; it remains in the series as published.
Five children with large-angle constant exotropia had strabismus surgery 6-12 months after LASIK; amblyopia therapy (occlusion, correction of residual error) resumed 1 month after LASIK.
BCVA, keratometry, topography, stereopsis and ocular alignment are reported; not extracted.
